I asked for it to design MMR that encourages people to PVP, gives hope for those who want to push for cosmetics and make it so players don’t just wait until the end of season to push rating.

It’s long, but has some really cool ideas!

—-

Below is a conceptual MMR and rating system geared to keep rated PvP engaging throughout the entire season, rather than feeling like a grind until the final weeks. The guiding principles are:
1. Steady Progression
2. Ongoing Incentives
3. Balanced Catch-up Mechanics

  1. Season Start and Partial Reset
    1. Soft MMR Reset
      • At the start of each season, lightly reduce everyone’s previous season’s MMR (for example by 5–10% instead of a full wipe).
      • This ensures top players still face stiff competition right away, but it also means that returning or mid-tier players don’t get buried at the bottom.
    2. Initial Placement Matches
      • Each player must play a small set (e.g., 10) of placement matches in the new season.
      • These placement matches are more “volatile” in that your MMR can swing more quickly than normal. This helps the system lock onto your skill level within fewer games.

Outcome: Everyone starts at an MMR that’s close to their skill from the prior season, preventing top-heavy or bottom-heavy extremes and helping the system converge on “fair” matchmaking earlier.

  1. Gradual Rating Inflation Each Week

Instead of having rating gains balloon only near the end of the season, implement scheduled incremental “rating inflation” throughout the season:
1. Weekly MMR Increment
• Every week (e.g., during maintenance), add a small, flat MMR boost (e.g., +10) to every active player’s MMR if they played a minimum number of rated matches that week (e.g., 5 matches).
• This helps newer or mid-tier players catch up gradually over the season, instead of facing steep rating differences until a sudden late-season inflation.
2. Bracket-Specific Adjustments
• If your bracket (2v2, 3v3, Solo Shuffle, etc.) is under-populated, the system could apply a slightly higher weekly boost to that bracket’s active players.
• This encourages participation in less active brackets and ensures each bracket remains healthy.

Outcome: The small, regular inflation means there’s always a reason to queue, because you won’t get left behind if you are consistently playing. It also prevents the “wait until end-of-season” mentality, since rating moves up in small increments over time.

  1. Rating Floors and Tiered Rewards

Rating Floors
• At specific rating thresholds (e.g., 1400, 1600, 1800, 1950, etc.), players who achieve that rating for the first time during the season unlock a rating floor—they can’t drop below that floor for the remainder of the season.
• Additionally, each floor may require a small number of wins at or above that threshold before it “locks in” (ensuring a real demonstration of skill rather than a one-time lucky streak).

Benefits:
• Players have a sense of progress—once they hit 1600 (for example) and lock it in, they will not fall below 1600. This removes the demoralizing effect of big rating losses after reaching a milestone.

Tiered Rewards and Titles
• Tiered Cosmetic Rewards (e.g., armor tints, illusions, mounts) for each rating bracket (1400, 1600, 1800, 1950, etc.) that visually evolve the higher you go.
• For example, at 1950, you unlock a unique transmog color variant. Pushing beyond that might earn an additional accent or glow effect.

Benefits:
• Instead of a single, end-of-season “hard push” for one reward, players see incremental, visually interesting rewards all season.

  1. Ongoing Participation Incentives

Weekly “Engagement” Quests
• Implement a weekly PvP quest (or “challenge”) that rewards a small, direct rating bonus or additional currency if you’ve played a certain number of rated matches (e.g., 10).
• This bonus could manifest as a small MMR spike (+5 or +10 for hitting the weekly milestone), or awarding a token to purchase PvP cosmetics.

Benefits:
• Ensures that active players keep inching upward and remain engaged.
• Adds a “safety net” for those who might have a losing streak—steady participation can still result in slow forward progress.

Seasonal Checkpoints
• Break the season into two or three “phases” (e.g., early/mid/late). At the end of each phase, players who have met certain participation thresholds (X matches played during that phase) gain a slight rating floor bump or MMR reset advantage going into the next phase.

Benefits:
• Resets any accidental stagnation. If you had rough luck in the early phase, you get a mild chance to re-calibrate for mid-season.

  1. Transparency and Clarity

Lastly, none of these changes succeed if the details are too mysterious. Provide a clear, in-game explanation (even in patch notes or tooltips) of how weekly MMR increments, rating floors, and tiered rewards work. Players feel more confident when they know how to engage with the system, and they’ll be more motivated to strive for the next milestone.

Summary

By combining:
1. Soft resets and quick MMR convergence at season start,
2. Gradual, predictable weekly inflation,
3. Rating floors (so players don’t lose all progress on a bad day),
4. Tiered rewards that give meaningful goals before the final push,
5. And clear communication around how gains and milestones work,

…you encourage consistent participation throughout the entire PvP season. Players can pursue transmog rewards like 1950 rating at a reasonable pace—without feeling compelled to “wait out” the season for a massive end-of-season inflation spike.

Competitive PvP Rating & Ranking System Design

Core Design Principles

  • Separate visible Rank from hidden MMR
  • Clear progression path for new players
  • Meaningful competition at all skill levels
  • No artificial inflation mechanics
  • Regular seasonal rewards without forcing daily play
  • Catch-up mechanisms that don’t devalue active play

Rating & Ranking Structure

Hidden MMR System

  • True skill-based matchmaking using an improved Glicko-2 system
  • More volatile for new players, stabilizing with more games
  • No artificial inflation or deflation
  • Used purely for matchmaking, not visible rewards

Visible Rank System

  • League-style tiered system with divisions
  • Tiers: Bronze, Silver, Gold, Platinum, Diamond, Master, Grandmaster
  • Each tier except Master/Grandmaster has 4 divisions (I-IV)
  • Points within divisions (0-100)
  • Master tier uses pure points system (similar to LoL’s LP)
  • Top 100 players qualify for Grandmaster tier

Rank Progression

  • Win/loss points determined by MMR difference between teams
  • Base points: +25/-25 for even matches
  • Maximum variance: +35/-15 for severe underdog wins
  • Point adjustments scale smoothly between these extremes
  • Promotion requires:
    • Reaching 100 points in current division
    • Winning 2 out of 3 promotion matches
  • Demotion occurs at 0 points with a loss
  • Demotion protection: 3 games after reaching new tier

Season Structure

Regular Season (10 weeks)

  • Weeks 1-8: Standard competitive play
  • Weeks 9-10: Final push period with special rewards
  • Weekly rewards for playing 10+ rated matches
  • No rating inflation, ever

End of Season

  • Soft reset based on final rank
  • Example reset structure:
    • Grandmaster → Platinum I
    • Master → Platinum IV
    • Diamond → Gold IV
    • Platinum → Silver IV
    • Below Platinum → Bronze I

Seasonal Rewards & Progression

Weekly Milestones

  • Complete 10 rated matches: Bonus currency
  • Win 5 matches: Additional rewards
  • No direct rating rewards to prevent inflation

Achievement System

  • Permanent achievements for first-time rank milestones
  • Special titles for consistent performance across seasons
  • Unique rewards for playing during “prime time” hours
  • Weekly featured achievements with bonus rewards

Seasonal Rewards

  • Base rewards determined by peak rank achieved
  • Additional rewards for:
    • Games played milestone tiers (50/100/200 games)
    • Maintaining rank for multiple weeks
    • Participation in underplayed brackets

Catch-up Mechanics

Performance-Based Acceleration

  • New players and returning veterans gain/lose more points
  • System accelerates players clearly below their skill level
  • Acceleration reduces as player approaches true skill level
  • No artificial rating inflation, just faster convergence

Activity Protection

  • Rank decay only applies to Master/Grandmaster
  • Lower ranks maintain position while inactive
  • Returning players get “comeback games” with accelerated gains
  • Protected from demotion for first 3 games back

Competitive Integrity Features

Queue Health

  • Role/spec-based matchmaking where applicable
  • Dynamic queue restrictions based on rank differences
  • Stricter matching during prime time hours
  • Relaxed matching during off-hours with adjusted rewards

Anti-Abuse Measures

  • Win-trading detection using pattern recognition
  • Stricter penalties for verified win-trading
  • MMR/Rank adjustments for participants in unfair matches
  • Regular review of top ladder for suspicious patterns

Implementation Notes

Technology Requirements

  • Real-time rating updates
  • Accurate MMR calculation system
  • Reliable match history tracking
  • Anti-abuse detection systems
  • Performance monitoring tools

User Interface Needs

  • Clear display of current rank and progress
  • Detailed match history with rating changes
  • Achievement and reward tracking
  • Season progress timeline
  • Personal statistics dashboard

Future Considerations

Potential Expansions

  • Tournament integration
  • Team ranking systems
  • Seasonal themes with unique rewards
  • Special event periods
  • Community challenges

Monitoring Metrics

  • Queue times by rank/time
  • Match quality ratings
  • Player retention rates
  • Rank distribution curves
  • Season participation patterns
